selectionScope: Preferred identity for refinement; original raster and implementation remain unapproved
scope: Film Programme homepage, desktop and mobile comparison board
prompt: Create a high-fidelity UX/UI DESIGN COMPARISON BOARD for Cinema Platform, a Ukrainian cinema website. This is an actual interface mockup, not a moodboard or poster, not code. Landscape board approximately 1800 by 1200. On the left show a large straight-on desktop homepage viewport with readable real interface regions (about 1240 by 930 at scale); on the right show a fully independent, correctly reflowed mobile homepage viewport (about 390 by 930 at scale), not a shrunken desktop. No perspective devices or computer props. Small neutral board label above each: Desktop, Mobile. BOTH views show the same Film Programme UX: visible navigation, film imagery and title, date context, clearly readable screening buttons directly beside/below that film, and the start of a second film entry below. Film-first editorial discovery, with integrated showtimes, never a uniform repeated card grid. Desktop and mobile opening viewport must include at least one usable-looking screening action without scrolling. Actual brand text "Cinema Platform". Ukrainian navigation "Фільми", "Розклад", "Квитки"; secondary "Увійти". Date "26 жовтня" and next-date choice "27 жовтня". Demo programme lead title "Дюна: Частина друга", secondary title "Памфір", third if space "Тіні забутих предків". Programme imagery: rich illustrative cinematic desert scene with a small cloaked figure, second film a photographic-looking rural Ukrainian forest scene. Imagery is illustrative not actual licensed movie stills. Lead screenings: "18:30 · Зал 1", "20:45 · Зал 2"; secondary "19:10 · Зал 1". Include small action "Усі сеанси". No prices, seat counts, availability guarantees, age ratings, screening formats, premiere dates, reviews, star ratings, recommendation claims, marketing statistics, or countdowns. Add a legible small footer outside both viewports: "Концепт · демонстраційна програма". Same content in both views. Exquisite polished typography and aligned meaningful controls; clear visual distinction between headings, metadata and actions. Keep text on solid contrasting surfaces, touch-sized mobile controls; text is not embedded illegibly over busy imagery. No decorative icon tiles, stock SaaS sections, glass panels, rounded card grid, gratuitous gradients or meaningless ornaments. Image must communicate actual homepage composition at finished visual fidelity. DIRECTION B — FESTIVAL SIGNAL. A sharply authored contemporary film-festival identity, purposeful modernist graphic typography, not a corporate blue SaaS dashboard. Solid saturated ultramarine #173FE5, clean chalk #F5F4EF, near-black #14181F, spare lemon #F3E45A for selected date/action. Hard edges, modular rules, zero card shadows, zero gradients. Typography: commanding tall condensed Cyrillic sans titles (Roboto Condensed-like), restrained highly readable Golos-like sans UI, large tabular session numbers. Desktop: bold ultramarine masthead spanning width with white Cinema Platform wordmark, horizontal white text navigation; beneath, an asymmetric chalk editorial field with enormous dark condensed title occupying left third and a wide natural-color desert image on right two-thirds. Crucially an integrated ultramarine screening strip runs below the title-and-image spread: explicit date at left and large lemon/white session actions at right; this is functional programme information not decorative banners. Below strip show the next film as a restrained chalk row with compact image and bold title/time; clear whitespace. A small editorial "ПРОГРАМА" kicker, no generic slogan. Mobile: cobalt masthead, visible navigation labels rather than hidden-only icons; compact selected-date strip, large title that wraps naturally, panoramic short desert image, extremely clear chalk/blue screening section with lemon selection action; second film begins below. Main image not full-screen. Make composition visually confident and graphic while remaining calm around reading and scheduling. Show a selected date through fill, underline and text, not color alone.
contentProvenance: Illustrative programme and generated film-like imagery; not retrieved catalogue content, actual screenings, or licensed film stills.
